long_biography.plain_text:
Malaysian financier Jho Low studied at Harrow and the Wharton School before building contacts with Gulf investors. His investment firm joined Sony, Mubadala and other partners in the acquisition of EMI Music Publishing. He also assembled a substantial art collection, including paintings by Claude Monet and a drawing by Vincent van Gogh.

His acquisitions later became the subject of international asset-recovery proceedings. A US federal judge entered civil forfeiture judgments in 2019 covering assets acquired by Low and his family. A further settlement in 2024 covered property and artworks, with proceeds destined for Malaysia. These civil agreements did not resolve the separate criminal proceedings against him.
